title: Personal Services Plan Suspension Length — First Month and Number of Months
content:
A Personal Services Plan suspension taken for as long as the package allows starts with a fixed first month and runs for a fixed number of whole calendar months, determined as follows.

## The first suspended month

The suspension runs for whole calendar months from the first calendar month whose first day is at least the package's suspension notice days after the request is signed. It ends on the last day of its last suspended month.

## The number of months

1. **One total.** The months a suspension may run are worked out as one total: the package's maximum suspended months per rolling 12 months, which is the starting allowance and not a ceiling, plus the months added for the plan's time in force, less the months counted for the plan's most recent recorded suspension. That total is never below zero, the floor being applied once to the final number of months and never to a part of it. The Personal Services Pay-As-You-Go Plan has nothing to suspend.
2. **Time in force.** Time in force adds 2 months where the whole months since the plan's effective date are at least 48, 1 month where they are at least 24 but fewer than 48, and nothing where they are fewer than 24.
3. **The most recent suspension.** Of the plan's most recent recorded suspension, the months that ended fewer than 12 whole months before the request are counted, and nothing is counted where the plan has none on record. Equivalently: take the calendar months the suspension covered, from its first suspended month to its last; the number counted is that figure or 12 less the whole months elapsed from the suspension's end date to the request, whichever is lower, and never below zero.
4. **Whole months.** Whole months are counted from the earlier date to the date of the request, a whole month elapsing on the same day of each later month.

## Time-in-force months

| Whole months since the plan's effective date | Months added |
|---|---|
| Fewer than 24 | 0 |
| 24 to 47 | 1 |
| 48 or more | 2 |

*Hypothetical boundary:* a plan effective 1 October 2022 has 48 whole months on a request dated 1 October 2026 (2 months added) and 47 on a request dated 30 September 2026 (1 month added).

## Worked examples (hypothetical inputs)

Taking for illustration a package whose starting allowance is 2 months, a plan effective 1 January 2025 (fewer than 24 whole months at every date below, so nothing added for time in force) and a most recent suspension covering May and June 2025 (ended 30 June 2025, 2 months):

| Request date | Whole months since 30 June 2025 | 12 less those months | Months counted | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 January 2026 | 7 | 5 | 2 | 0 |
| 29 June 2026 | 11 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| 30 June 2026 | 12 | 0 | 0 | 2 |

**Floor on the total.** With the same 2-month allowance, nothing added for time in force and a most recent suspension of 3 months that ended 2 whole months before the request (3 counted): 2 less 3 would be below zero, so the total is 0. With the plan 30 whole months in force instead, the total is 2 plus 1 less 3, which is 0; at 48 whole months it is 2 plus 2 less 3, which is 1.

**First month (hypothetical notice of 7 calendar days):** a request signed on 25 May — 1 June is 7 days later, so June is the first suspended month; a request signed on 26 May — 1 June is only 6 days later, so the first suspended month is July. A 2-month suspension from 1 July ends on 31 August.
